A_target.statement:
[[Definition:Beta Reduction|$\beta$-reduction]] in the [[Definition:Untyped Lambda Calculus|untyped $\lambda$-calculus]] is [[Definition:Confluent Relation|confluent]]:
:$t \twoheadrightarrow_\beta u \land t \twoheadrightarrow_\beta v \implies \exists w: u \twoheadrightarrow_\beta w \land v \twoheadrightarrow_\beta w$

B_source.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Relation|relation]] with the [[Definition:Diamond Property|diamond property]]:
:$a \mathrel R b \land a \mathrel R c \implies \exists d: b \mathrel R d \land c \mathrel R d$
Then the [[Definition:Transitive Closure of Relation|transitive closure]] $R^+$ is [[Definition:Confluent Relation|confluent]].

substitutions.the auxiliary relation with the diamond: parallel reduction, contracting several redexes simultaneously
substitutions.the one-step diamond: the confluence of two parallel reduction steps in a single step each

derived.the tiling of a diagram of steps: a grid of parallel reduction squares

object_map.reformulation: Replace the given relation by an auxiliary one that closes in a single step, then take its transitive closure.

validity_conditions: Ordinary beta-reduction does not itself have the one-step diamond property, since one step can duplicate a redex the other has already contracted; this is exactly what parallel reduction repairs.
Parallel reduction sits between one-step and multi-step beta-reduction, so its transitive closure is precisely multi-step reduction.
The diamond property for parallel reduction is proved by induction on the term structure, using a complete development that contracts all residual redexes at once.
proof_plan: Define [[Definition:Parallel Reduction|parallel reduction]] $\Rightarrow$, which contracts any set of [[Definition:Redex|redexes]] of a term simultaneously.

We have:
:$\to_\beta \subseteq \Rightarrow \subseteq \twoheadrightarrow_\beta$
Hence the [[Definition:Transitive Closure of Relation|transitive closure]] of $\Rightarrow$ is $\twoheadrightarrow_\beta$.

By [[Principle of Structural Induction|induction]] on terms, using the complete development $t^*$:
:$t \Rightarrow u \implies u \Rightarrow t^*$
Hence $\Rightarrow$ has the [[Definition:Diamond Property|diamond property]].
